blocks.text: Box-Cox transformation automated the search for an optimal reshaping power, but it genuinely carried forward one real limitation from Log Transformation before it, requiring strictly positive input values. Yeo-Johnson transformation closes that exact gap, extending the same automated, maximum likelihood driven search to genuinely handle zero and negative values as well, completing this module distribution reshaping toolkit.

This topic covers the genuinely real datasets where Box-Cox simply cannot be applied at all, how the Yeo-Johnson formula branches to handle positive and negative values separately while staying controlled by the same single lambda parameter, the practical choice between the two techniques in scikit-learn, and a full recap of this entire Feature Scaling module now that both its major families of technique are complete.
1. Real Datasets Box-Cox Genuinely Cannot Handle

blocks.alt: Real Datasets Box-Cox Genuinely Cannot Handle
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142158-333477226.png

Many genuinely common real world variables include zero or negative values as a normal, expected part of their range, not as an error to be cleaned away. Temperature measured in Celsius genuinely includes negative values below freezing. Profit or loss figures genuinely include negative values whenever a loss occurs. A delta feature, the change between two values, something that connects directly back to the aggregation and date features covered earlier in this course, can genuinely be zero or negative just as easily as positive.

Every one of these genuinely common, real cases was completely out of reach for both Log Transformation and Box-Cox, not due to some oversight, but because their underlying formulas mathematically require strictly positive input to even be computed at all.
2. How the Yeo-Johnson Formula Handles Both Signs

blocks.alt: How the Yeo-Johnson Formula Handles Both Signs
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142158-617511091.png

Yeo-Johnson genuinely branches its formula based on the sign of x itself, values that are zero or positive follow a Box-Cox style branch, closely related to the formula covered in the previous topic, while genuinely negative values follow a separate, mirrored branch built specifically to handle them. Both branches, importantly, remain controlled by the exact same single lambda parameter, keeping the technique unified rather than treating positive and negative values as two entirely disconnected problems.

This branching structure is genuinely the key mathematical insight that makes Yeo-Johnson work, rather than trying to force one single formula to cover the entire real number line, which the Box-Cox formula genuinely cannot do, it defines two coordinated pieces that together cover every possible input value.
3. A Worked Example
Applying Yeo-Johnson to a genuinely realistic profit and loss column, one that Box-Cox could never accept directly, shows this extended capability in action.

code.content:
from sklearn.preprocessing import PowerTransformer
import pandas as pd

profit_loss = pd.DataFrame({
    "monthly_result": [1200, -300, 4500, -50, 800, -1200, 15000],
})

transformer = PowerTransformer(method="yeo-johnson")
transformed = transformer.fit_transform(profit_loss)

print(pd.DataFrame(transformed, columns=profit_loss.columns))
print("Lambda found:", transformer.lambdas_)

blocks.text: This monthly_result column genuinely mixes positive and negative values, a column that Box-Cox would have genuinely rejected outright, yet Yeo-Johnson handles it directly in a single call, finding its own optimal lambda across the full real number line.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Just like Box-Cox, always store the fitted PowerTransformer object, or its lambda values, alongside a trained model. Both the forward and inverse transform genuinely depend on it for any real prediction to make sense.

blocks.text: 4. The Practical Choice in scikit-learn
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142158-688828526.png

scikit-learn PowerTransformer genuinely offers both techniques through a single interface, choosing method box-cox for strictly positive data, or method yeo-johnson for data that genuinely might include zero or negative values. Passing genuinely positive-only data to the box-cox method works exactly as covered in the previous topic, while passing any data containing zero or negative values to that same method genuinely raises an error.

The yeo-johnson method, by contrast, genuinely never raises that particular error, since it was built specifically to accept the full real number line, making it a genuinely safe, universal default whenever there is any uncertainty about whether a feature might include zero or negative values.

blocks.text: 5. When to Choose Yeo-Johnson Over Box-Cox

blocks.alt: When to Choose Yeo-Johnson Over Box-Cox
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142159-321312366.png

Whenever a feature genuinely contains, or might ever contain, zero or negative values, Yeo-Johnson is genuinely the only valid choice between the two, Box-Cox simply cannot be applied at all in that case. When a feature is genuinely, reliably strictly positive, both techniques work, and the choice becomes more a matter of genuine convention or preference than a hard requirement.

A genuinely reasonable, safe default in practice is to reach for Yeo-Johnson first whenever there is any real uncertainty about a feature future range, since it never fails on positive-only data either, it simply behaves equivalently to Box-Cox in that specific case.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: When genuinely unsure whether a feature might contain zero or negative values now or in the future, default to Yeo-Johnson. It never fails where Box-Cox would work, and it additionally covers the cases Box-Cox genuinely cannot.

blocks.text: 6. The Same Underlying Search, Extended
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142159-747946067.png

It is genuinely worth being explicit that Yeo-Johnson is not a completely different idea from Box-Cox, it uses the exact same maximum likelihood search process covered in the previous topic, searching for the lambda that makes the transformed data most genuinely normal, just applied across a formula that has been extended to cover the full real number line rather than only the positive half of it.

Holding onto this connection matters, log transformation, power transformation, Box-Cox, and Yeo-Johnson are genuinely not four separate, unrelated techniques to memorize independently, they form one single, continuous idea, progressively generalized across these four topics, from one fixed transformation to a fully automated, universal one.
7. Recapping This Entire Feature Scaling Module

blocks.alt: Recapping This Entire Feature Scaling Module
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142159-849288130.png

This module genuinely covered two distinct families of technique. Standardization, Normalization, Robust Scaling, and Min-Max Scaling all genuinely rescale features linearly, changing their scale and boundaries while leaving the underlying distribution shape completely untouched. Log Transformation, Power Transformation, Box-Cox, and now Yeo-Johnson instead genuinely reshape a distribution itself, correcting skew rather than simply rescaling.

Both families are genuinely necessary in a real, well built pipeline, and they are not mutually exclusive either, a genuinely skewed feature is often first reshaped with something like Yeo-Johnson, and then standardized afterward, addressing shape and scale as two genuinely separate, complementary concerns.

blocks.text: 8. Yeo-Johnson Versus What Comes Next
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142369-567949649.png

With Yeo-Johnson, this Feature Scaling module reaches a genuinely complete close, every numeric feature, regardless of its original scale, sign, or skew, now has a clear, established path to becoming genuinely well prepared for the algorithms covered later in this course. Numeric preparation, though, is only genuinely half the picture, most real datasets also contain categorical features that still need their own dedicated treatment.

The next module, Encoding Techniques, addresses exactly that remaining gap, covering how to genuinely turn categorical data, city names, product categories, yes or no flags, into the kind of numeric representation every algorithm covered later in this course actually requires.

items: Yeo-Johnson extends the Box-Cox idea to genuinely handle zero and negative values, unlike log or Box-Cox alone.
Real variables like temperature, profit or loss, and deltas genuinely require this extended capability.
The formula genuinely branches by the sign of x, with both branches controlled by the same lambda.
scikit-learn PowerTransformer offers both methods; yeo-johnson is genuinely the safer, more universal default.
Yeo-Johnson uses the genuine same maximum likelihood search as Box-Cox, just extended across the full real number line.
This module covered two families: linear rescaling and distribution reshaping, often used together in a real pipeline.
